after.description: The `next` cursor from the previous page. Opaque. Ignored without page_size.

breakdowns.description: JSON-encoded array of dimensions to break down by, NOT a comma-separated string. Valid dimensions are "type" (by usage type) and "team" (by project). Pass `["type"]` for per-usage-type series, or `["type","team"]` for per-project series within each usage type. Team breakdowns require "type"; do not pass `["team"]` by itself. Omit for a single aggregate series. Sending a bare string like "type,team" will fail with a 400 error.

end_date.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Pass this whenever start_date is set; use today's date if the user did not name one.

interval.description: Time bucket size, one of "day" or "week". Default "day".

page_size.description: Return at most this many series, ranked by total, with a `next` cursor for the page after. A caller that pages never approaches the size this endpoint refuses oversized breakdowns at. Requires a project breakdown.

start_date.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). For open-ended investigations, choose an explicit recent window such as the last 30 days. If you use "all", also pass end_date.

team_ids.description: JSON-encoded array of numeric team (project) IDs to filter by, NOT a comma-separated string. Pass as e.g. `[1,2]`. Omit for every project this request can see: all org teams for full billing-access callers, or the member's visible/project-scoped teams for member read-only callers.

top_projects.description: Maximum number of projects to return, ranked by total spend, when breakdowns includes "team". The projects beyond it are folded into one "All other projects (N)" series rather than dropped, so the totals still add up to the real bill. Ignored without a team breakdown. Omit it to get every project, which is the default and the right choice for most questions. Set it only when an organization has enough projects that the full response is unwieldy, and say so in your answer, because a limited response names only the largest spenders.

usage_types.description: JSON-encoded array of usage type identifiers to filter on, NOT a comma-separated string. Pass as e.g. `["event_count_in_period"]` or `["event_count_in_period","recording_count_in_period"]`. Omit for all usage types.
